prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 221, Part A gate (docs/seismology-gate): power spectrum, background, numax and Delta nu, and a mass and radius through the scaling relations
committed: before any prototype, before any oracle output and before any spectrum of any light curve was computed or looked at, on this branch (docs/seismology-gate); the prototype is on spike/seismology-gate and is never merged. The Kepler files were fetched (SHA-256 below) and their headers listed; no flux was plotted, binned or transformed before this file was committed.
rule: A threshold that proves unmeasurable fails the gate on that threshold; only Carl resets one. A threshold is never re-read after a result is seen: an alternative reading is recorded as a question for Carl. Verdicts are by the rule under verdict, not by judgement afterwards.

published.star: KIC 10318430 (Kp 12.03; a low-luminosity red giant on the red-giant branch, observed in all of Kepler quarters 0 to 17)
published.source: Yu et al. 2018, ApJS 236, 42 (arXiv:1802.04455), Tables 1 and 2 as printed in the paper, read 2026-10-30

teffK.origin: Mathur et al. 2017 through Yu et al. Table 2

published.analysis: the SYD pipeline on the 17 to 18 quarter long-cadence series (1318.2 d in the paper's length column); formal uncertainties by 200 chi-squared perturbations; 1.0 and 0.5 per cent added in quadrature to numax and Delta nu only when propagating to mass and radius

solarReferences.origin: Yu et al. 2018 Sec. 3.3 (SOHO/VIRGO analysed like the Kepler data)

relationScatter.citations: Huber et al. 2017, ApJ 844, 102 (arXiv:1705.04697): seismic radii accurate to about 5 per cent or better for 0.8 to 8 Rsun and no significant offset for low-luminosity RGB stars (about 3 to 8 Rsun); Gaulme et al. 2016, ApJ 832, 121: against ten red giants in eclipsing binaries the relations overestimate radii by about 5 per cent and masses by about 15 per cent on average
relationScatter.contractChoice: the stated interval of a mass adds an independent relation scatter of 10 per cent (fractional, in quadrature) and of a radius 5 per cent: this is the contract's choice between the two citations, not a citation; the 15 per cent mean mass excess of Gaulme et al. is a bias the interface states in words and does not subtract

systematicFloors.origin: Yu et al. 2018 Sec. 3.5, added in quadrature to the formal uncertainties

data.source: Kepler long-cadence light curves (PDCSAP_FLUX, SAP_QUALITY, TIME, CADENCENO), MAST, https://archive.stsci.edu/missions/kepler/lightcurves/0103/010318430/ , retrieved 2026-10-30, HTTP 200 for every file, 7.2 MB in 18 files, fetched by the coordinator; NASA mission data public at MAST, acknowledgement requested
data.subset: Q9 to Q12 (four consecutive quarters, about one year: the series a student receives, chosen here by file number, before any spectrum existed); the full series is Q0 to Q17 (the published solution's data)
data.negativeReal: the 30-minute-bin EK Draconis TESS sector 16 pack of Prompt 220 (a young active dwarf; 1,055 rows, one sector): the same cadence as Kepler long cadence, a dwarf whose solar-like numax lies far above the Nyquist frequency

preprocessing.selection: SAP_QUALITY == 0 and finite PDCSAP_FLUX and finite TIME; per quarter, flux divided by its median and turned into ppm (1e6 (F/median - 1)); quarters joined with no jump correction
preprocessing.highPass: a running median over 99 consecutive valid cadences (about 2.0 d, cutoff near 5.7 uHz) within each quarter, subtracted; a 4.5-sigma clip on the MAD-based sigma, applied once
preprocessing.grid: the cadence number (CADENCENO) places every point on the even cadence grid dt = 1765.5 s (29.4244 min); a missing cadence is set to zero after the mean is removed (zero-filled) and the spectrum is divided by the duty cycle N_valid/N
preprocessing.domain: numax from 20 uHz to 0.8 of the Nyquist frequency (about 226 uHz): outside it no mass and no radius are returned (the high-pass removes the signal below, the sinc attenuation and the unresolved aliasing above)

powerSpectrum.definition: single-sided power spectral density in ppm^2 per uHz normalised so that Parseval holds: the sum of PSD x delta_nu over 0 to Nyquist equals the variance (ppm^2) of the series. FFT of an evenly sampled series x_n of N points spaced dt seconds: P_k = 2 dt |X_k|^2 / N x 1e-6 (X_k the unnormalised DFT; k = 1 to N/2 - 1; the k = 0 and Nyquist bins halved), divided by the duty cycle for zero-filled gaps. A white series of variance sigma^2 has the level 2 sigma^2 dt x 1e-6 ppm^2/uHz; a sine of amplitude A on a full grid peaks at N dt A^2 / 2 x 1e-6
powerSpectrum.gaps: the periodogram for gaps is the least-squares sinusoid fit (a cos + b sin on the mean-subtracted data) at each frequency, with power density (a^2 + b^2) / 2 x N_valid dt x 1e-6: it has the same white level and the same sine peak, with the same units, so an FFT and a periodogram of the same series are comparable

backgroundModel.form: B(nu) = eta(nu)^2 sum_{i=1,2} [2 sqrt(2)/pi] a_i^2 / b_i / (1 + (nu/b_i)^4) + W, eta = sinc(pi nu / (2 nu_Nyq)); the envelope adds eta^2 H exp(-(nu - numax)^2 / (2 s^2)) on top (Kallinger et al. 2014 form; the white term W is not attenuated)
backgroundModel.statistic: the Whittle likelihood: -ln L = sum_k [ ln M_k + P_k / M_k ] over 10 uHz to the Nyquist frequency (the spectrum of a Gaussian series scatters as chi-squared with two degrees of freedom about its model)
backgroundModel.optimiser: Nelder-Mead on the log of each parameter from a fixed grid of starts, the best likelihood kept; a parameter reported on a bound is a flag, and the share of such fits is leg C2

numaxMethod.snr: the spectrum divided by the background-only part of the fitted model
numaxMethod.smoothing: Gaussian with FWHM = 2 Dnu_emp(nu), Dnu_emp(nu) = 0.263 nu^0.772 uHz (Stello et al. 2009, ApJ 700, 1589; the same empirical relation sets the Delta nu search window), iterated to a fixed point from the envelope fit's numax
numaxMethod.estimate: the location of the maximum of the smoothed SNR spectrum, refined by a parabola through three points
numaxMethod.detection: the envelope fit improves 2 (ln L1 - ln L0) by at least 40 over the background-only model (three extra parameters; chosen as a trial-adjusted p of order 1e-6) with numax inside the domain, AND the comb is significant (below)

deltaNuMethod.window: numax +- one FWHM of the fitted envelope (FWHM = 2.355 s)
deltaNuMethod.acf: the autocorrelation of the mean-subtracted SNR spectrum inside the window, as a function of lag; Delta nu is the lag of the highest peak of the lightly smoothed ACF (Gaussian sigma = 0.02 Dnu_emp) inside 0.6 to 1.4 Dnu_emp(numax), refined by a parabola
deltaNuMethod.combSignificance: 400 seeded shuffles of the SNR bins inside the window (the same ACF peak search on each): the comb is significant when fewer than 1 per cent of the shuffles reach the observed peak height
deltaNuMethod.uncertainty: the standard deviation of numax and Delta nu over 200 seeded chi-squared (2 dof)/2 perturbations of the spectrum with the background held fixed, in quadrature with the systematic floors above

massRadius.propagation: Monte Carlo, 4000 seeded draws through the scaling relations (Prompt 154's propagation), with independent Gaussian numax, Delta nu, Teff, numax_sun and Dnu_sun; the interval is the 16th to 84th percentile of the draws, widened by the relation scatter above; correlations between numax and Delta nu are neglected (stated)

ensemble.generator: an independent Python generator written for the oracle, never the kernel: a stochastic spectrum drawn as complex Gaussian Fourier coefficients with variance equal to the model power density (so the periodogram scatters exactly as chi-squared with two degrees of freedom), inverse-transformed to a time series of N = 16000 cadences, and masked with the valid-cadence pattern of the real Q9 to Q12 series
ensemble.model: granulation: a1 = a2 = 3382 numax^-0.609 ppm, b1 = 0.317 numax^0.970, b2 = 0.948 numax^0.992 uHz (Kallinger et al. 2014 relations as the generator's design values, labelled); white W in {2, 6, 20} ppm^2/uHz; envelope: radial orders n with nu_n0 = Dnu (n + eps), eps = 0.634 + 0.63 log10 Dnu, quadrupole at nu_n0 - 0.121 Dnu, dipole at nu_n0 + Dnu/2 (no mixed modes: stated limit of the generator and of the method), Lorentzian linewidth 0.15 uHz, visibilities V0 = 1, V1 = 1.5, V2 = 0.6 (squared in height), Gaussian envelope FWHM 0.66 numax^0.88 uHz (Mosser et al. 2012), radial-mode amplitude A = 39 (numax/155)^-0.84 ppm so that the power per order is of the order of the published value; Dnu = 0.263 numax^0.772 (1 + 0.03 z), z standard normal; sinc attenuation applied

legs.what: an FFT spectrum of a bin-centred noise-free sine (A = 100 ppm, N = 4096) peaks at N dt A^2/2 (x1e-6); a periodogram of the same sine with 10 per cent seeded gaps at an off-grid frequency peaks at N_valid dt A^2/2
Parseval on the FFT spectrum of seeded white and coloured series, 30 seeds: the integral of the spectrum equals the variance
the mean FFT power density of 20 seeded white series (N = 8000) over 5 to 270 uHz equals 2 sigma^2 dt
FFT (zero-filled, duty-corrected) and the periodogram on the same gapped white series (20 seeds, 10 per cent gaps in 12-cadence runs): the mean power density over 5 to 270 uHz agrees
the kernel's FFT spectrum of 3 seeded series against an independent numpy rfft implementation of the normalisation above

the kernel's gap periodogram against astropy.timeseries.LombScargle (version recorded; fit_mean False, center_data True, normalization psd, converted to the density above) on a seeded gapped series at 500 frequencies
the same comparison on the real Q9 to Q12 series after pre-processing, 400 frequencies between 5 and 270 uHz; the astropy values are pinned as a fixture
on the 200-spectrum ensemble the fitted background-only part at the true numax against the true background: the median and 90th percentile of |ratio - 1|
the share of ensemble fits with any parameter on a bound
numax recovery on the ensemble: |numax_hat/numax - 1|
Delta nu recovery on the ensemble: |dnu_hat/dnu - 1|
the share of the 200 ensemble spectra detected (envelope and comb significant)

coverage of the 68 per cent interval of numax on the ensemble, the interval being the formal one (the standard deviation over the 200 perturbations, without the systematic floors) (a test of the interval's construction, stated as such: the generator is independent of the kernel but the likelihood is the generator's own statistic)
coverage of the 68 per cent interval of Delta nu on the ensemble, the formal interval as in F2
the scaling relations with the published numax, Delta nu and Teff and the solar references give the published uncorrected mass and radius

coverage of the stated 68 per cent mass interval on the ensemble, the truth being the relation value of the true numax and Delta nu times (1 + 0.10 z) with z a seeded standard normal, and Teff = 4800 K +- 150 K assumed known to its stated sigma
the same for the radius with the relation scatter 0.05

200 seeded spectra of a non-oscillating dwarf (granulation and white only, the solar numax lying above the Nyquist frequency, same masks and levels): none may be reported as detected beyond 2 per cent
the real EK Draconis 30-minute TESS series (dwarf) returns not detected
100 seeded ensemble spectra with true numax of 8 to 18 uHz or 240 to 270 uHz: no mass and no radius is returned for any
KIC 10318430, Q9 to Q12, pre-processed as committed, against the published solution: numax, Delta nu, mass and radius (published Teff and solar references)
KIC 10318430, Q0 to Q17: the same comparison with the same limits

classes.note: E1 and E2 are scored by field: detected counts with deltaNu; mass and radius are scored in massRadius

verdict.A: every leg passes: numax, Delta nu, mass and radius through the scaling relations with their intervals, the FFT added to js/numeric/
verdict.B: every leg of the classes spectrum, background, negatives and deltaNu passes and at least one leg of numax or massRadius fails: Delta nu and the comb only, no mass and no radius (the FFT is added with its validation)
verdict.C: any leg of the classes spectrum, background, negatives or deltaNu fails: no inference; a reading step on what the oscillations show; no FFT added to js/numeric/

bytes: measured and reported (the kernel's gzipped size and the real-data sidecar); T3 has no deferred allocation, so the measured overrun is raised exactly under the standing approval of 2026-10-10 and is not a verdict leg

amendments.when: 2026-10-30, on this branch, before the spike's first line was written and before any spectrum was computed
amendments.what: the coverage legs F2 and D3 score the formal interval (the perturbation standard deviation, no systematic floors) and their upper bound moves from 0.85 to 0.90; G2 and G3, whose stated interval includes the systematic floors and the relation scatter, have their upper bound moved from 0.85 to 0.95; no lower bound and no other leg moves
amendments.why: the 200 perturbations multiply an already scattered spectrum by a second chi-squared(2)/2 draw, which doubles the variance of the logarithm of every bin, so a correct implementation has a formal interval about 1.4 sigma wide and a coverage near 0.84 at the nominal 0.68, and the floors (0.5 per cent in Delta nu, a quantity the self-consistent ensemble measures to better than that) widen it further; an upper bound of 0.85 would fail a correct implementation by construction. The upper bounds guard only against intervals so wide that coverage is meaningless; the lower bounds (0.60) are the test against over-confidence and are unchanged.

amendments.when: 2026-10-30, on this branch, before any spectrum was computed (the oracle's reference fixtures for the sine legs had been generated, no kernel output compared)
amendments.what: A1.sine: the bound of the gapped sine moves from 1e-6 to 1e-2 against the analytic N_valid dt A^2/2; the exact comparison of the gap periodogram with an independent least-squares fit stays in B2 and B3 at 1e-6
amendments.why: the committed definition subtracts the mean of the valid points before the sinusoid fit; for a pure sine on a gapped grid that mean is not zero, so the fitted amplitude differs from A by a relative amount of order 1e-3 (the constant's projection on the cosine and sine columns), and the analytic peak can not be reached to 1e-6 by the definition itself. The leg's purpose is the units and the N_valid dt normalisation, which 1e-2 tests; no other leg moves.
